terminal_name: Monfalcone LNG Logistics Terminal (new-terminal candidate, this batch)
issue: The only annual-volume figure found for this candidate terminal -- 'circa 1 miliardo di metri cubi' portato a terra (adriaports.com, sponsor's own project page; verified tokens '400 ISO' and 'miliardo di metri cubi' both PASS) -- does not carry a stated time basis on the source page and does not reconcile with the only concrete commercial figure available, a supply deal for 'massimi 400 ISO-container' of LNG (same page). 400 x 40-ft ISO containers (~17-18 t LNG each) is a small fraction of what 1 billion standard m3/y of gas would require if shipped this way; the 1 bcm figure reads as an aspirational full-buildout target for the logistics scheme (mother-ship + shuttle-vessel + dock), not a corroborated operating throughput. No second independent source was found that explains what the figure measures. This is exactly the class of capacity-basis error the batch was asked to watch for (cf. the live-DB Port of Vlora FSRU 2 record, whose Capacity is currently ~1e9x too large).
suggested_action: Capacity left BLANK on the staged new_terminals record (see italy.newterminals.json) with the ambiguity explained in italy.disc.wiki.json. If a future pass finds a clean, dated, per-year throughput figure for this specific facility (not the mother-ship's storage volume, not a multi-year cumulative, not a full-buildout aspiration), stage it then with a proper [ref]. Do not backfill a number now on inference alone.
